description: Structured backlog of systemic dispatcher findings produced by Phase 8 self-review. Upsert by finding_id; bump recurrence + last_seen when a finding re-appears. Do not rewrite from scratch.

findings.title: Subagents run git ops in the dispatcher working tree instead of a dedicated worktree, leaving local commits ahead of remote
evidence: Phase 5 reviewer for PR#661 ran git ops in /home/user/property-management, creating a local commit ahead of remote
PR#640 rebaser likely did the same
Recurring issue tracked as #7
findings.proposed_fix: Hard-isolate every subagent to its own `git worktree add` under .claude/worktrees/<task>; have the dispatcher refuse to spawn any subagent that would operate in the dispatcher CWD.

findings.title: Concurrent subagent pushes to dev create rapid version-bump cycles and empty the dispatcher Phase 6 commit
evidence: Version churn 0.2.964 -> 0.2.968 in a single run from concurrent subagent pushes
Dispatcher Phase 6 commit was 'nothing to commit' because subagents pre-empted all changes
findings.proposed_fix: Serialize state writes behind a single owner: subagents return diffs, only the dispatcher commits/pushes assignments + version.

findings.title: Phase 6 archive append is not idempotent — re-archiving an already-archived task_id appends a duplicate row inside assignments-archive.json
findings.symptom: Self-test T4 FAIL — 4 task_ids present twice (active=0, archive=2 each)
evidence: 561874d5: dispatcher-self-test T4 FAIL — duplicate task_id: gap-10b-5-support-data-ui, gap-82-4-swiftui-listing-detail-impl, gap-82-5-swiftui-inquiries-account, pm-data-support-data-tracking-events
Verified each is active=0 / archive=2 — duplicated WITHIN assignments-archive.json, not an active->archive leak (so T18/T19 pass while T4 fails)
6bf8e883 Phase 6 archive-split: 'merged with origin/dev state' — the merge re-appended rows already archived by a concurrent run
findings.root_cause: Phase 6 merges this run's terminal rows into the archive by append rather than upsert-by-task_id; when a concurrent run or a prior cycle already archived the same task_id, the row is appended again instead of being deduped.
findings.proposed_fix: Phase 6 archive write must upsert by task_id (group_by(.task_id) | map(last)) before persisting assignments-archive.json. Add a self-test T18b that fails when archive contains duplicate task_ids (currently T4 catches it cross-file but the in-archive case is the actual bug). dispatcher-prompt.md Phase 6 archive-split step.

findings.title: Dispatcher self-test FAILs on most runs (new rows missing hardening fields / duplicate archive rows), reducing it to a backfill-after-the-fact ritual
findings.symptom: Self-test fails at end of run, then state is hand-patched ('-> now backfilled')
evidence: 6bf8e883: 'self-test: T11 FAIL (5 new rows missing hardening fields -> now backfilled)'
561874d5: T4 FAIL (4 duplicate archive task_ids)

b8bf30ad (this run): T4 FAIL again — gap-10a-1-oauth-tests, gap-10b-3-admin-health-ui present in BOTH active (in-progress, this run) and archive (merged #470/#471 on 2026-05-25). Distinct root cause from the in-archive dup — see reclaim-of-already-merged-task-id.
Pattern: self-test is run AFTER state is written, so failures are repaired reactively rather than prevented; FAIL now recurs 2+ consecutive runs on different T-numbers (T11 -> T4 -> T4)
findings.root_cause: Hardening fields and archive dedup are enforced only by the post-hoc self-test, not by the Phase 3 claim / Phase 6 archive writers themselves, so every claim/archive cycle can introduce a fresh violation.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the T11 (hardening fields) and T4 (archive dedup) invariants into the write path: Phase 3 claim template must stamp all hardening fields; Phase 6 must upsert-dedup before write. Keep the self-test as a gate but make it pass on first run. Add a Phase 6 pre-commit hook that runs dispatcher-self-test.sh and aborts the commit on FAIL.
findings.affected_artifact: .research/dispatcher-prompt.md (Phase 3 claim template + Phase 6 pre-commit self-test gate)

findings.title: Both rebaser subagent and dispatcher increment rebase_attempts, double-counting the counter
evidence: rebase_attempts landed on 2 instead of 1; caught and fixed manually
findings.proposed_fix: Assign a single owner for rebase_attempts mutation (either rebaser OR dispatcher, never both) and document it in the rebaser contract.

findings.title: Two dispatcher cycles overlap with no lock, forcing a mid-run reset + re-run on push conflict
evidence: A parallel run pushed state (generated=2026-05-28T12:32:35Z, 137 archived) mid-transition; reset to origin/dev and re-ran
d654512a 2026-05-28 02:15: 'R0 new (all captured by concurrent run)' — Phase 5 verdicts for #643/#641/#642 produced by a concurrent dispatcher
6bf8e883 2026-05-28 14:11: archive-append re-merged rows already archived by a concurrent run (root of T4 duplicate-archive FAIL)
b8bf30ad 2026-05-28 15:17: re-claimed gap-10a-1/gap-10b-3 that a concurrent/prior run had already merged into archive 12h earlier — a lock would have surfaced the completed state before claim
findings.proposed_fix: Take a run-level advisory lock at Phase 1 (dispatcher.lock ref/row or GitHub deployment lock); abort fast if held. This also prevents the archive-dedup and stale-base re-run failures which are downstream symptoms of overlap.

findings.title: Phase 5.5 merger strands approved PRs on diverse blockers (ci-fail, needs-human-review, draft, ci-unknown, dirty) with no per-blocker routing
evidence: 5 approved PRs unmergeable: #633 ci-fail, #639 needs-human-review, #641 draft+needs-human-review, #643 ci-unknown/0-checks, #640 dirty
0 merged by dispatcher; approved pool only grows
db36d8e5 2026-05-28 08:08: X=0 merged-now with 2 merge-attempts (PR#632, PR#650) and PR#643 stuck on ci-green-prefix anomaly

b8bf30ad 2026-05-28 15:17: M0 merge-attempts / X0 merged-now; 'Approved+blocked: PR#639, PR#641 (needs-human-review; no merge attempt)' — same two PRs still stranded across runs with no escalation routing
findings.proposed_fix: Per-blocker routing in Phase 5.5: ci-fail -> Phase 5.7 respawn; needs-human-review -> explicit human-escalation tag + stop; dirty -> auto-rebase; ci-unknown/0-checks -> re-trigger CI or wait, don't strand.

findings.title: PRs with zero reported CI checks are neither pass nor fail and the merger has no rule, leaving them stuck
evidence: PR#643 had CI=unknown / 0 checks; merger silently left it stuck
db36d8e5 2026-05-28 08:08: 'Anomaly: PR#643 reviewer_summary=ci-green-prefix (not verdict=approve/changes); stuck until head changes'
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit ci-unknown/0-checks branch to the merge gate: re-trigger CI (or wait + recheck) rather than treating absent checks as indeterminate-and-stranded. Also normalize reviewer_summary to a verdict= key so a 'ci-green-prefix' note is not mistaken for a verdict.

findings.title: Resuming from a compacted context forces re-derivation of every phase decision via live API, slow and divergence-prone
evidence: Run resumed from a summary after context compaction; all phase decisions re-derived via GitHub API checks
findings.proposed_fix: Persist a small per-run decisions ledger in management state so a post-compaction resume reloads decisions instead of re-deriving them.

findings.title: Suffix-variant task_ids (-impl/-fix/-v2) bypass the dedup gate and open a second PR for the same gap
evidence: gap-82-4-swiftui-listing-detail (PR#641) and gap-82-4-swiftui-listing-detail-impl (PR#644) both in review simultaneously
Phase 7 dup-skip log keys on exact task_id; -impl variant slipped through and got its own PR
005d5154 2026-05-28 11:13: 'Dup-skip: gap-82-4-swiftui-listing-detail reason=open-pr conflicts_with=#641,#644' — suffix variants again collided after the fact
findings.proposed_fix: Normalize task_id by stripping trailing -impl|-fix|-v\d+ before the open-PR / same-epic conflict check, or key dedup on the gap-id prefix (gap-82-4-*) so suffix variants collide. T20 already computes this stem for active rows — reuse the same stem function in the Phase 2/3 dedup gate.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget implementer spawns lose the row<->PR link, leaving orphaned PRs back-filled in Phase 2
evidence: Phase 2 reconciliation discovered 4 orphaned PRs this run (#685, #686, #687, #641) with no assignment rows
Reconciliation/orphan noise present in 2 of the 3 visible runs
005d5154 2026-05-28 11:13: 'Implementers spawned (fire-and-forget): ... gap-81-1-report-schedule-edit-ui (stale-already merged)' — spawned an implementer for an already-merged gap
findings.proposed_fix: Write the assignment row (status=in-progress, branch set) BEFORE firing the implementer, so a PR can never be orphaned. Also re-check remote merge state immediately before spawn to avoid spawning for already-merged gaps. Keep Phase 2 reconciliation as a safety net only.

findings.title: Post-merge review cadence gate uses file mtime, which a fresh clone resets to now — gate never fires after a clone
evidence: Phase 7: 'Post-merge: skipped (mtime < 24h — fresh clone reset mtime)'
findings.proposed_fix: Persist last_post_merge_review_at in management state (e.g. assignments.json meta) and gate Phase 6 on that timestamp rather than file mtime — immune to clone resets.

findings.title: Local dev branch drifts behind origin/dev, forcing a mid-run reset + re-run
evidence: Phase 7 note: 'Local dev was 50 commits behind origin/dev; reset to origin/dev and re-ran.'
2026-05-28T13:41Z: parallel run pushed state mid-transition; reset to origin/dev and re-ran phases
6bf8e883 2026-05-28 14:11: Phase 6 archive-split 'merged with origin/dev state' — base drift again forced a remote-state merge
b8bf30ad 2026-05-28 15:17: claim of already-merged gap-10a-1/gap-10b-3 indicates the claim pool was read from a base that did not reflect the archive's merged state
findings.proposed_fix: At run start, git fetch and (when N commits behind) reset --hard origin/dev before any gate, so timing-sensitive phases run against current base on the first pass.

findings.title: Review->merge conversion is bursty: merge attempts fail and merged-now swings wildly run-to-run
evidence: Merge attempts: PR#633 merged=false ci-failed; PR#639 merged=false needs-human-review
Merged-now trend across runs: 1 -> 0 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0 -> 2 -> 11 -> 11 (X across 7ceb1481..6bf8e883) — bursty, dispatcher M=0 on the two 11-merge runs (all human/concurrent merges)
2026-05-28T13:41Z: dispatcher merged 0 of 5 approved PRs (all blocked); only human merges drained the pool
b8bf30ad 2026-05-28 15:17: X0 merged-now, M0 merge-attempts (prior run X11) — extreme run-to-run swing continues; dispatcher again contributed 0 merges
findings.proposed_fix: Track per-PR merge-blocker reason (ci-failed vs needs-human-review) as a metric; consider Phase 5.7-style auto-respawn on ci-failed and explicit human-escalation tagging for needs-human-review so the review pool drains steadily.

findings.title: Commit-subject metrics trailer omits dup-skip volume, undercounting run activity for trend reads
evidence: Subject: C2 R4 M2 X0 F0 A12 — but Phase 7 recorded 4 dup-skips not surfaced in the trailer
Prior report (2026-05-28T09-47-03Z) already noted metrics-trailer drift (X2 vs 4 actually merged)
005d5154 2026-05-28 11:13: subject 'X11 merged-now' but Phase 7 body also recorded 1 Dup-skip + 1 Dropped not in the trailer
findings.proposed_fix: Recompute the metrics trailer after Phase 5.5 (post-merge) and add a dup-skip count token so commit subjects match the Phase 7 summary.

findings.title: Phase 3 claim re-claims a task_id that is already merged in the archive, scheduling already-shipped work and breaking self-test T4
findings.symptom: Self-test T4 FAIL — gap-10a-1-oauth-tests and gap-10b-3-admin-health-ui each present in BOTH active (in-progress, claimed this run) and archive (merged). Also surfaces in goal-check as GC1 done_with_open_gap=10.
evidence: b8bf30ad Phase 7 'Claimed: gap-10a-1-oauth-tests, gap-10b-3-admin-health-ui' at 2026-05-28T15:17:09Z
Archive already holds gap-10a-1-oauth-tests merged=PR#470 (merged_at 2026-05-25T00:45Z) and gap-10b-3-admin-health-ui merged=PR#471 (merged_at 2026-05-24T20:51Z) — work shipped ~12h before re-claim
dispatcher-self-test T4 FAIL: 'a row exists in both active and archive — Phase 6 move bug'
goal-check.sh GC1-referential-integrity FAIL includes done_with_open_gap=10 — coverage gaps marked done but still re-opened/claimable, the same class of bug at the coverage layer
findings.root_cause: The Phase 2.6 buffer / Phase 3 claim selection picks claimable gaps from the coverage/action-list pool without subtracting task_ids already terminal in assignments-archive.json. A merged-then-still-open coverage gap (done_with_open_gap) re-enters the claimable set, so the dispatcher claims a fresh in-progress row for an already-merged task_id.
findings.proposed_fix: In Phase 3 claim selection, exclude any candidate whose task_id (and its normalized stem) already appears with a terminal status in assignments-archive.json before stamping an in-progress row. Reconcile coverage 'done' state against archive merges in Phase 2.6 so a merged gap cannot remain claimable (fixes goal-check done_with_open_gap). Add self-test assertion that a newly-claimed task_id has no terminal archive twin.

findings.title: goal-check GC1 referential-integrity FAILs with 105 orphan action-list items referencing nonexistent coverage entries
findings.symptom: goal-check.sh GC1-referential-integrity FAIL — observed orphans=105, done_with_open_gap=10 (expected 0/0). First run where goal-check.sh actually executes (prior run it was SKIP/not-found), immediately red.
evidence: bash .research/goal-check.sh: 'FAIL GC1-referential-integrity — observed=orphans=105 done_with_open_gap=10 expected=orphans=0 done_with_open_gap=0'
b8bf30ad Phase 7: 'goal-check: GC1-referential-integrity=FAIL'
Prior run 6bf8e883: 'goal-check: SKIP (goal-check.sh not found)' — the gate was effectively absent until this run, so accumulated coverage/action-list drift went unmeasured
done_with_open_gap=10 overlaps the reclaim-of-already-merged-task-id root cause (merged gaps still flagged open)
findings.root_cause: action-list.json carries 105 items whose coverage reference no longer exists in coverage.json (coverage entries removed/renamed without cascading to action-list), plus 10 coverage gaps marked done while still open. The newly-added goal-check.sh exposes a backlog of referential drift that was never enforced before.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Phase 2.6 cascade step that prunes/relinks orphan action-list items when coverage entries change, and reconciles coverage done-state against archive merges. Make goal-check.sh GC1 a Phase 6 gate (record-only first, enforcing once the 105-item backlog is drained). Triage the existing 105 orphans into prune-vs-relink as a one-time cleanup.

findings.title: goal-check GC3 buffer-bounds FAILs — claimable=117 is ~2x the upper bound of 60 after a +30 Phase 2.6 refill
findings.symptom: goal-check.sh GC3-buffer-bounds FAIL — observed claimable=117 (open=134, dep_blocked=17), expected 18<=claimable<=60. Buffer nearly double the ceiling.
evidence: bash .research/goal-check.sh: 'FAIL GC3-buffer-bounds — observed=claimable=117 (open=134 dep_blocked=17) expected=18<=claimable<=60'
6bf8e883 Phase 2.6: 'Buffer refilled +30 items (coverage rubric 2026-05-28) | claimable=142/159' — refill ran with no upper-bound guard
b8bf30ad subject: 'B152/159 dep-blocked=7' — buffer continues to sit far above the 60 ceiling run-to-run
self-test T15 also reports open_claimable=117 — consistent with goal-check
findings.root_cause: Phase 2.6 buffer refill targets a minimum (top-up to keep work flowing) but has no maximum cap, so a single large coverage-rubric refill (+30) pushed claimable well past the GC3 ceiling of 60. The refill step does not consult GC3 bounds before adding items.
findings.proposed_fix: Make Phase 2.6 refill bound-aware: stop refilling once claimable reaches the GC3 upper bound (60), and refill only up to that cap. Optionally drain excess by deferring lowest-score claimable items back to backlog rather than holding them claimable. Wire GC3 bounds as the single source of truth shared by refill and goal-check.
